# 1 Samuel Chapter 4 -- The EMET Bible (Literal)
**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A), Folios 133v-134r | **Source Image:** source-texts/hebrew-OT/1SA_004_page_001.jpg, 1SA_004_page_002.jpg

---

**4:1** And-was [the]-word of-Samuel to-all Israel. And-went-out Israel to-meet the-Philistines for-battle, and-they-encamped by Even-ha-Ezer [the Stone of Help], and-[the]-Philistines encamped in-Aphek.

**4:2** And-arrayed [the]-Philistines to-meet Israel, and-spread-out the-battle, and-was-struck Israel before [the]-Philistines, and-they-struck in-the-array in-the-field about four thousand man.

**4:3** And-came the-people to the-camp, and-said [the]-elders of-Israel, "Why has-struck-us YHWH today before [the]-Philistines? Let-us-take to-ourselves from-Shiloh the-ark of-[the]-covenant of-YHWH, and-let-it-come in-our-midst, and-let-it-save-us from-[the]-palm of-our-enemies."

**4:4** And-sent the-people [to]-Shiloh, and-they-carried from-there the-ark of-[the]-covenant of-YHWH of-hosts, [who]-sits [upon the]-cherubim. And-there [were the]-two sons of-Eli with [the]-ark of-[the]-covenant of-God, Hophni and-Phinehas.

**4:5** And-it-was as-[the]-coming of-[the]-ark of-[the]-covenant of-YHWH to the-camp, and-shouted all Israel a-great shout [teruah], and-resounded the-earth.

**4:6** And-heard [the]-Philistines the-voice of-the-shout and-said, "What [is the]-voice of-the-shout, the-great, the-this, in-[the]-camp of-the-Hebrews?" And-they-knew that [the]-ark of-YHWH had-come to the-camp.

**4:7** And-feared [the]-Philistines, for they-said, "God has-come to the-camp." And-they-said, "Woe to-us! For there-has-not been like-this yesterday [and the]-day-before.

**4:8** Woe to-us! Who will-deliver-us from-[the]-hand of-these-Gods, the-mighty-ones? These [are] the-Gods who-struck Egypt with-every plague in-the-wilderness.

**4:9** Strengthen-yourselves and-be men, [O]-Philistines, lest you-serve the-Hebrews as-they-served you. And-be men and-fight!"

**4:10** And-fought [the]-Philistines, and-was-struck Israel, and-they-fled each-man to-his-tent. And-was the-slaughter very great, and-fell from-Israel thirty thousand foot-[soldiers].

**4:11** And-[the]-ark of-God was-taken, and-[the]-two sons of-Eli died, Hophni and-Phinehas.

**4:12** And-ran a-man of-Benjamin from the-array, and-he-came [to]-Shiloh on-that-day, and-his-garments [were]-torn and-earth upon his-head.

**4:13** And-he-came, and-behold, Eli [was]-sitting upon the-seat by-[the]-side of-the-road, watching, for his-heart was-trembling concerning [the]-ark of-God. And-the-man came to-declare in-the-city, and-cried-out all the-city.

**4:14** And-heard Eli the-voice of-the-cry, and-said, "What [is the]-voice of-the-tumult, the-this?" And-the-man hurried, and-came and-declared to-Eli.

**4:15** And-Eli [was a]-son of-ninety and-eight years, and-his-eyes stood [i.e., were fixed/set], and-he-was-not able to-see.

**4:16** And-said the-man to Eli, "I [am] the-one-coming from the-array, and-I from the-array fled today." And-he-said, "What was the-thing, my-son?"

**4:17** And-answered the-one-bearing-tidings and-said, "Fled Israel before [the]-Philistines, and-also a-great slaughter was among the-people, and-also your-two sons died, Hophni and-Phinehas, and-[the]-ark of-God was-taken."

**4:18** And-it-was as-he-mentioned the-ark of-God, and-he-fell from-upon the-seat backward by-[the]-side of-the-gate, and-was-broken his-neck, and-he-died, for old [was] the-man and-heavy. And-he had-judged Israel forty years.

**4:19** And-his-daughter-in-law, [the]-wife of-Phinehas, [was]-pregnant, about-to-give-birth. And-she-heard the-report of-[the]-being-taken of-[the]-ark of-God, and-[that]-died her-father-in-law and-her-husband, and-she-knelt and-gave-birth, for turned-upon-her her-labor-pains.

**4:20** And-at-[the]-time of-her-dying, and-spoke the-women standing-over-her, "Do-not-fear, for a-son you-have-borne." And-she-did-not answer, and-she-did-not set her-heart [upon it].

**4:21** And-she-called the-lad I-chabod [Ikavod], saying, "Gone-into-exile [is the]-glory from-Israel," concerning [the]-being-taken of-[the]-ark of-God, and-concerning her-father-in-law and-her-husband.

**4:22** And-she-said, "Gone-into-exile [is the]-glory from-Israel, for was-taken [the]-ark of-God."

---
## EMET's Textual Notes

1. **4:1 -- textual division**: The Leningrad Codex begins 4:1 with "And was the word of Samuel to all Israel." The LXX and 4QSam-a include additional text here, placing this clause as the conclusion of chapter 3 and adding material about the Philistines assembling for war. EMET follows the Leningrad verse division.

2. **4:1 -- Even-ha-Ezer** (אֶבֶן הָעֵזֶר): "The Stone of Help." This is a different location from the Eben-ezer of 1 Samuel 7:12, which Samuel names after a later victory. The narrator uses the name proleptically or refers to a different site.

3. **4:4 -- "sits [upon the] cherubim"** (ישֵׁב הַכְּרוּבִים): This epithet for YHWH of hosts describes Him enthroned above the cherubim on the ark's mercy seat. The participle יוֹשֵׁב ("sitting/dwelling") functions as a divine title.

4. **4:8 -- "these Gods... in the wilderness"**: The Philistines confuse the plagues of Egypt with events "in the wilderness." This reflects their imperfect knowledge of Israelite tradition -- an authentic narrative detail. The plural "Gods" (אֱלֹהִים) reflects the polytheistic perspective of the Philistines.

5. **4:9 -- "lest you serve the Hebrews as they served you"**: The Philistines' fear of enslavement echoes the reversal theme of Hannah's song (2:4-8). The Leningrad Codex reads כַּאֲשֶׁר עָבְדוּ לָכֶם ("as they served you"), which some take as referring to Israelite servitude under the Philistines.

6. **4:13 -- "by the side of the road, watching"**: The Leningrad Codex reads דֶּרֶךְ מְצַפֶּה, with Eli positioned beside the road watching for news. His anxiety about the ark (not about his sons) characterizes his piety despite his failures.

7. **4:15 -- "his eyes stood"** (קָמוּ עֵינָיו): Literally "his eyes rose/stood" -- an idiom for eyes becoming fixed or set, indicating blindness. This connects to 3:2 where his eyes "began to grow dim."

8. **4:18 -- "forty years"**: The notice that Eli judged Israel forty years connects Samuel to the Judges framework. The number forty is a conventional period in biblical chronology.

9. **4:21 -- Ichabod** (אִי־כָבוֹד): The name is explained by the narrator as meaning "no glory" or "where is the glory?" The prefix אִי functions as a negation: "not-glory" or "alas-glory." The woman's naming act, like Rachel's naming of Ben-oni (Gen 35:18), is a death-bed theological statement.

10. **4:19-22 -- the wife of Phinehas**: Her response to the news is structured in descending order of significance: the ark (mentioned first and last), then her father-in-law, then her husband. The ark's capture, not personal loss, is what drives her to name the child "the glory has departed."

-- EMET
